status: evaluation-only taxonomy -- NOT wired into any production code path (CQAS ranking, Learning Extraction, Review Cycle) as of this freeze. Used by a human expert reviewer (or a future structured-LLM-judge step) to label findings AFTER a real Phase I-B1 review. v2 finalizes naming/coverage at the close of the Phase I-B0 Retrospective Proxy Evaluation series (Hungary/BC Strategy/Iran/US-China) and aligns every label to the Hypothesis Register (H1-H6).

generation_miss.definition: An expert-important dimension/point does not appear in ANY of the CQAS candidates generated (not merely mis-ranked -- absent from generation entirely).
generation_miss.source: pre-existing Phase G CQAS signal, reused unchanged

ranking_miss.definition: An expert-important dimension exists somewhere among the generated candidates, but not within the displayed Top N.
ranking_miss.source: pre-existing Phase G CQAS signal, reused unchanged

selection_miss.definition: An expert-important dimension was within the displayed Top N, but the human user did not select the candidate carrying it (only meaningful when a REAL user made the selection -- not applicable to Phase I-B0's operational-proxy selection).
selection_miss.source: pre-existing Phase G CQAS signal, reused unchanged
selection_miss.note: Not evaluated in Phase I-B0/I-B0.1/I-B0.2/I-B0.3; first usable in Phase I-B1 with a real selector.

validated_candidate.definition: An expert-important dimension IS present, generated, ranked in the displayed Top N or Design, matching the expert's own emphasis.
validated_candidate.source: pre-existing Phase G CQAS signal, reused unchanged

investigation_question_reframing.definition: AI's investigation_question is the raw input theme carried forward verbatim, with no distinct analytical significance-framing added, where the expert's own practice was to add such framing.
investigation_question_reframing.source: H4 -- strongest retrospective finding, 4/4 cases, 3/3 independent case families

actor_selection_miss.definition: A named actor/entity the expert treated as materially important is absent from AI's key_actors list (Design or CQAS candidate), independent of whether the surrounding scenario/dimension itself was captured.
actor_selection_miss.source: H1 -- preliminary/inconclusive, severity/shape inconsistent across families

observable_indicator_miss.definition: A specific, concrete observable indicator the expert used or would use (e.g. a named military deployment, a numeric threshold, a named legal/institutional trigger) is absent from AI's watch_points/observable_indicators, even when the broader topic area is present.
observable_indicator_miss.source: H2 -- preliminary, n=1 independent family (BC Strategy/Iran)

absence_anomaly_miss.definition: Missing/omitted information that the expert treated as an analytical signal in itself (not what IS present, but what is conspicuously NOT present -- a missing actor, missing statement, missing sector, missing expected action/signal) is not treated as a signal by AI at all. Distinct from generation_miss: this is not about a topic/dimension being absent from generation, it is about failing to reason from an absence in the INPUT/evidence itself.
absence_anomaly_miss.source: H6 -- new, preliminary but high-quality evidence (n=1 independent family, US-China, but LESS affected by the evidence-scarcity caveat than other labels since the signal was present directly in the T0 input text)

rejection_logic_miss.definition: A hypothesis/scenario the expert explicitly considered and rejected IS generated by AI as a candidate, but the expert's REASON for rejecting it (often an actor-specific behavioral/psychological constraint, e.g. face-saving) is absent -- AI presents the same content as a live, undismissed alternative.
rejection_logic_miss.source: H3 (refined) -- multi-hypothesis generation itself is NOT weak (see US-China counter-evidence); the specific gap is explicit rejection reasoning, especially actor-behavioral

scenario_ranking_divergence.definition: AI's own main_scenario (selected/Rank1) does not match the expert's actual conclusion, even though the expert-consistent content exists elsewhere in the candidate set (e.g. as an alternative_scenario). The candidate existed; what differed was ranking/selection, not generation.
scenario_ranking_divergence.source: H5a -- preliminary, n=1 (Iran/M086, the only case with genuine Selection Logic ground truth), confidence capped due to sparse retrieval evidence

evidence_weighting_gap.definition: The relative weight AI assigns to competing pieces of evidence when choosing between scenarios does not match how the expert weighted the same (or analogous) evidence -- e.g. treating a weak/generic indicator as equally decisive to a specific, expert-prioritized one.
evidence_weighting_gap.source: H5b -- preliminary, n=1, confidence capped due to sparse retrieval evidence

expert_unique_insight.definition: A finding/dimension that is not merely 'missed' by AI but reflects genuine domain judgment not obviously derivable from the retrievable evidence at all (distinguishes 'AI should have found this' from 'no system could reasonably have found this without the expert's own private judgment'). MUST arise naturally from the expert's own review -- never elicited by a leading question (see review_design_notes.h6_non_leading_rule below).
expert_unique_insight.source: carried over from the original Phase I-B spec Section 10 taxonomy

ai_review_miss.definition: In the AI-assisted Review stage (not reached by Phase I-B0/I-B0.1/I-B0.2/I-B0.3), a finding a real expert reviewer catches that the existing AI/Reviewer-support mechanism did not flag.
ai_review_miss.source: maps to the original Phase I-B spec Section 10 'AI Review Effectiveness' categories (AI detected / AI partially detected / AI missed / AI false positive / expert unique insight)

design_miss.definition: A broader Analysis Design field (analytical_lenses, evidence_needed, knowledge_gaps, report_structure) that the expert's real work implies as necessary is absent or weak, distinct from the narrower labels above.

draft_reasoning_miss.definition: In the Draft/Report stage, a reasoning defect matching the existing 11-axis Draft quality rubric (Question Fit, Evidence Sufficiency, Fact/Inference Separation, Reasoning Strength, Actor Logic, Alternative Hypotheses, Scenario Coherence, Timeline, Confidence Calibration, Knowledge Gaps, Decision Utility) that the expert would flag.

hypothesis_register_mapping.H5c_rejection_logic_in_ranking_context: rejection_logic_miss (same label, applied within a scenario-ranking review question rather than a standalone-nuance review question)
hypothesis_register_mapping.H5d_actor_behavioral_reasoning: rejection_logic_miss + actor_selection_miss combined (review design should ask separately, see review_design_notes.h5_decomposed_questions)

review_design_notes.h5_decomposed_questions: Per the governing instruction, Phase I-B1's Expert Review should not just collect free-form comments for scenario ranking -- it should explicitly elicit, for the AI-presented candidate set: (1) which scenario the expert considers most likely, (2) why they would adopt it, (3) why they would NOT adopt each of the others, (4) what would need to change for the ranking to change. This lets H5a (Ranking) / H5b (Evidence Weighting) / H5c (Rejection Logic) / H5d (Actor Behavioral Reasoning) be scored as SEPARATE fields per candidate rather than collapsed into one vague 'is this a good scenario' rating.
review_design_notes.h6_non_leading_rule: Per the governing instruction, the Expert Review UI/script must NOT prompt the expert to 'look for what's missing' or otherwise hint at absence-detection. absence_anomaly_miss / expert_unique_insight may be labeled ONLY when the expert raises a missing actor / missing stakeholder / missing statement / missing sector / missing expected action / missing expected signal unprompted. A structured review form should leave open-ended comment space rather than a checkbox list of 'things that might be missing', to avoid contaminating this specific measurement.

confidence_requirement: Every label application must carry a confidence value (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW or MEDIUM-HIGH etc.) whenever the underlying T0 evidence reconstruction was not fully complete (see AsOfEvaluationClient audit_report per case, where applicable to a Phase I-B1 case that also uses the as-of harness).
